title: The tool vocabulary: one naming rule for two servers
status: GhydraMCP conforms; the x64dbg side does not yet (its 80 tools are flat PascalCase)

rule.shape: namespace_verb: snake_case, lower case, the first token names the domain
rule.why: The prefix is load-bearing, not decoration. Two tools that read memory exist and they mean different things: `memory_read` reads the static image Ghidra has open, and a live-process read must not be reachable by the same name. The namespaces also keep an agent's tool-selection bounded, which is why both servers group their tools.
rule.reserved_parameters_why: `arguments` is the name of the container the MCP protocol uses for a tool's parameters; a client that re-encodes the container loses the value, and the tool then runs with its defaults instead of failing. It happened here (x64dbg_call), and a guard now refuses the name.

ghydra_side.evidence: contract/tools.json (generated): every one of the 134 names matches the pattern, and no tool declares a reserved parameter

local_namespaces.kuna: drives the Kuna CLI; takes no instance
local_namespaces.x64dbg: drives the debugger's own MCP plugin; the prefixed names never collide with the static side

x64dbg_side.adoption: Rename in the registry, and keep the old names as aliases for one release: an agent configuration that names SetBreakpoint must not break the day the rule lands.
x64dbg_side.mapping_rule: Split the PascalCase into words, lower-case them, join with underscores, prefix `x64dbg_`.

collisions_that_matter.why: Same verb, different object: the image on disk versus the live process. An agent that confuses them reports a value that was never in the running program.
Ghidra's function and the debugger's view of a function differ by relocations and by what the debugger has symbols for.
A program is a file; a module is a loaded image of one. The TargetDescriptor is where the two are correlated.
